titulo: Reheating rice that sat out all afternoon doesn't fix it
receta: El que lo hace mal / pilar cocina; adaptado de 034-arroz-recalentado
destinatario: Se lo manda alguien que cocina a su roommate o su papá, el que deja la olla de arroz toda la tarde en la mesada, para decirle que recalentarlo de noche no lo arregla.

interaccion.guardar: Leftovers: fridge within 2 hours (1 hour if it's over 90 F), eat within 3-4 days, reheat to 165 F.
interaccion.comentar: How many hours does your rice usually sit out? Give me a number.

fuentes: USDA FSIS: Leftovers and Food Safety (fsis.usda.gov)
CDC MMWR 1994: Bacillus cereus food poisoning associated with fried rice at two child day care centers, Virginia, 1993

frases.texto: You left the pot of rice on the counter all afternoon, and tonight you're reheating it.
Raw rice can carry bacterial spores, and those spores can survive cooking.
If the rice sits out, the bacteria can multiply and make a toxin that reheating may not destroy. A CDC report traced an outbreak to fried rice held that way.
The USDA says refrigerate leftovers within two hours, or within one hour if it's over ninety degrees.
Then eat them within three to four days, and reheat to one sixty-five. Save this: two hours, three to four days, one sixty-five.
Heads up: reheating isn't the problem. The time the rice spent sitting out is.
So be honest: how many hours does your rice sit out? Give me a number.
Send this to the friend who leaves the rice pot on the counter all afternoon.
